source: World Health Organization (WHO) Fact Sheets + Primary Care

conditions.name: Acidity / Gastritis (Indigestion)
conditions.overview: Stomach lining irritation or acid reflux causing upper stomach pain, nausea, or chest discomfort after meals.

conditions.name: Anaemia (Low Haemoglobin)
conditions.overview: Anaemia is a condition in which the number of red blood cells or the haemoglobin concentration within them is lower than normal. It mainly affects women and children.

conditions.name: Asthma / Breathing Allergy
conditions.overview: Asthma is a chronic lung disease affecting people of all ages. It is caused by inflammation and muscle tightening around the airways, which makes it harder to breathe.

conditions.name: COVID-19 / Viral Respiratory Illness
conditions.overview: COVID-19 is the disease caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus. It usually spreads between people in close contact.

conditions.name: Chest / Heart Warning (Needs Urgent Check)
conditions.overview: Chest pain or breathing trouble can sometimes indicate a serious heart or lung issue and should be evaluated promptly by a doctor.

conditions.name: Chikungunya (Fever & Joint Pain)
conditions.overview: In symptomatic patients, CHIKV disease onset is typically 4–8 days (range 2–12 days) after the bite of an infected mosquito. It is characterized by an abrupt onset of fever, frequently accompanied by severe joint pain....

conditions.name: Common Cold & Cough
conditions.overview: Mild upper respiratory viral infection causing runny nose, sneezing, sore throat, and cough. Usually improves with rest and fluids.

conditions.name: Dehydration / Heat Exhaustion
conditions.overview: Loss of body fluids and salts causing dizziness, weakness, headache, and fatigue, especially after fever, vomiting, or loose motion.

conditions.name: Dengue
conditions.overview: Dengue (break-bone fever) is a viral infection that spreads from mosquitoes to people. It is more common in tropical and subtropical climates.

conditions.name: Ear Infection
conditions.overview: Common middle or outer ear infection causing ear pain, mild fever, or dizziness, often following a cold.

conditions.name: Eye Infection / Allergy (Conjunctivitis)
conditions.overview: Irritation or infection of the eye causing redness, itching, watering, or mild eye pain.

conditions.name: Food Poisoning / Stomach Infection
conditions.overview: Common digestive illness from contaminated food or water causing loose motion, vomiting, and stomach cramps. Hydration (ORS) is important.

conditions.name: Hepatitis B / Liver Infection
conditions.overview: Hepatitis B is an infection of the liver caused by the hepatitis B virus. The infection can be acute (short and severe) or chronic (long term).

conditions.name: High Blood Pressure (Hypertension)
conditions.overview: Hypertension (high blood pressure) is when the pressure in your blood vessels is too high (140/90 mmHg or higher). It is common but can be serious if not treated.

conditions.name: Jaundice / Hepatitis A
conditions.overview: Unlike hepatitis B and C, hepatitis A does not cause chronic liver disease but it can cause mild to severe symptoms and rarely fulminant hepatitis (acute liver failure), which is often fatal. However, infection does not...

conditions.name: Joint Pain / Arthritis
conditions.overview: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic disease that causes inflammation around the body and commonly presents with pain in the joints.

conditions.name: Kidney / Urinary Health Issue
conditions.overview: Kidney disease is often asymptomatic until late stages, which is why regular testing is important for people at risk. In advanced or severe kidney disease, symptoms may include fatigue, breathlessness, generalized...

conditions.name: Lower Back / Muscle Pain
conditions.overview: Low back pain (LBP) describes pain between the lower edge of the ribs and the buttock. It can last for a short time (acute), a little longer (sub-acute) or a long time (chronic). It can affect anyone.

conditions.name: Malaria
conditions.overview: Malaria is a life-threatening disease spread to humans by some types of mosquitoes. It is mostly found in tropical countries. It is preventable and curable.

conditions.name: Seasonal Flu (Viral Fever)
conditions.overview: Seasonal influenza (the flu) is an acute respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses. It is common in all parts of the world. Most people recover without treatment.

conditions.name: Skin Allergy / Rash (Dermatitis)
conditions.overview: Common skin reaction to allergens, heat, or irritation causing redness, itching, bumps, or rash.

conditions.name: Throat Infection (Tonsillitis / Pharyngitis)
conditions.overview: Irritation or infection of the throat causing throat pain, difficulty swallowing, cough, or mild fever.

conditions.name: Tuberculosis (TB) — Persistent Cough
conditions.overview: Tuberculosis (TB) is an infectious disease that most often affects the lungs. TB is caused by a type of bacteria. It spreads through the air when infected people cough, sneeze or spit.

conditions.name: Typhoid Fever
conditions.overview: Salmonella Typhi lives only in humans. Persons with typhoid fever carry the bacteria in their bloodstream and intestinal tract. Symptoms include prolonged high fever, fatigue, headache, nausea, abdominal pain, and...

conditions.name: Urinary Tract Infection (UTI)
conditions.overview: Common urinary infection causing burning or discomfort while urinating, lower stomach pain, or fever.

conditions.name: Viral Fever
conditions.overview: Common short-term fever caused by viral infection, often accompanied by body ache, headache, and tiredness.
